rationale: A wins because it is more disciplined about what the release actually gives you and what will stall a reporter. Its strongest line is "Wise says stablecoin rails are cheaper — the open question is who keeps the savings," which turns the public-company fact into a real tension instead of another stablecoin-adoption wrapper. B has good bones, but "building stablecoin settlement into a core product" quietly upgrades the fact pattern from a rollout to product centrality, and that is how founders end up pitching a story they cannot prove.
gaps_in_A: "which bank fees and float revenue get squeezed" is plausible, but the update does not establish float revenue exposure; keep it as a question, not a premise.
"stablecoin settlement is crossing into regulated, mainstream B2B money movement" needs external trend evidence. Wise is one strong data point, not the whole crossing.
The decay labels are a little too confident. "24hr" and "week" read precise without evidence from the update.
It should ask for expected share of Wise's £30B quarterly volume moving through stablecoin settlement more prominently; that is the scale proof reporters will want.
gaps_in_B: "One of the biggest cross-border payment networks" is comparative ranking language the update does not prove. £30B per quarter shows scale, not rank.
"building stablecoin settlement into a core product" overstates the fact pattern. The update says Wise is launching stablecoin settlement for business payments, not that it is core to the product.
"specific stablecoin and regulatory partner" invents a type of partner. The update says the stablecoin and partner are unnamed; it does not say the partner is regulatory.
"approved in some markets, not others" is directionally likely but still unsupported without a launch-market list. A policy reporter will not let that slide.
